description: Revocation is NOT rotation (#134). Rotation is orderly succession — the old binding still governed its era. Revocation INVALIDATES a binding as of the revocation's ANCHOR time: artifacts anchored before that point stay valid, artifacts anchored at/after are no longer governed by it (and, with no successor, are ungoverned → rejected). The revocation is its OWN anchored statement class (schema kya.pq_key_revocation.v0), naming the binding it revokes by content-address and PQ-authorized by that binding's key — see pq-key-binding-v0.revocation.json (deep lane). Effective time is the revocation's anchor time, NEVER a self-declared field (same reason cutoff uses anchor time, not created_at), so the vector supplies revocation_anchor_time rather than trusting the statement. Uses a DEDICATED example binding (964af387…) so the production genesis/rotation chain is untouched. Run: `python3 cutoff_enforce.py pq-key-binding-v0.revocation-vectors.json`. The revocation fills the revoked_at slot resolve_in_force already honours — the predicate built at #132 took revocation with no rewrite, same dividend as rotation.

cases.name: after binding, BEFORE revocation → governed (stays valid)
exactly AT revocation anchor time → no longer governed
pre-revocation post-cutoff, valid companion under the (then-live) key → admit
post-revocation post-cutoff, valid companion under the REVOKED key → still rejected (binding is gone)
